# Code of conduct — DRAFT

**Proposed community policy. Adoption, responsible maintainers and private
reporting contacts require owner approval before this policy becomes active.**

## Participation

Make collaboration welcoming and respectful for people of all backgrounds,
identities and levels of experience. Discuss ideas and technical work with care,
accept constructive feedback and acknowledge the effect of your words and actions.
Respect people's time, privacy and boundaries.

Harassment, threats, discriminatory or demeaning language, sexual harassment,
deliberate intimidation and publishing someone's private information without
permission are unacceptable. Do not retaliate against someone for raising a
concern or participating in its review. Good-faith technical disagreement is
welcome; personal attacks and repeated disruption are not.

## Scope

The proposed policy covers project issues, pull requests, discussions and other
official community spaces, including conduct while publicly representing the
project. It applies to contributors and maintainers alike.

## Private reporting and enforcement

- Private conduct reporting channel: **[PENDING: owner-approved private channel]**.
- Responsible maintainers and backup: **[PENDING: owner-approved public roles]**.
- Independent escalation for conflicts of interest: **[PENDING: private channel
  and reviewer role]**.
- Acknowledgement and appeal process: **[PENDING: response windows and procedure]**.

Do not put sensitive conduct reports or personal details in public issues. Until
a private contact is published, request a private contact without disclosing the
incident publicly. Security vulnerabilities use the separate
[security reporting policy](SECURITY.md).

The proposed process limits report access to those needed to assess and respond.
A reviewer with a conflict of interest must step aside. Reviewers should consider
context, impact and repeated behavior, explain decisions to affected people
where appropriate, and provide the approved appeal route. Possible responses
include a request to stop, content removal, a warning, temporary restrictions or
removal from project spaces. Enforcement authority and procedures remain pending
adoption; this draft does not name a current enforcement team.
